newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia forex intervention at $1.0 bln - report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia forex intervention at $1.0 bln - report.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said the bank sold one billion dollars in the forward market last week to stabilise the rupiah during a recent speculative attack.

Djiwandono was quoted by the Jakarta Post daily as saying the amount was less than the Thai and Philippines central banks sold to defend their currencies because the bank had taken pre-emptive action by widening the dollar-rupiah band.
Bank Indonesia widened its intervention band to 12 percent from eight percent on July 11. The band allows the central bank to intervene in the market if rates fall out of the band.

Djiwandono said the dollars were sold in the forward market and not in the spot market in order to protect the country's foreign exchange reserves. These were estimated at $21.08 billion at the end of June.
